reference: GNU coreutils tr, invoked by system Bash with the harness C locale (LC_ALL=C) and UTC environment. Parity expectations are generated independently by that GNU command; byte and error cases use small literal inputs.
coverage: Bash metadata: tr is a builtin and help tr succeeds.
Range translation and POSIX lower/upper classes.
Octal NUL deletion and octal escaped range translation over binary stdin.
Complemented translation including NUL and 0xff bytes in the C locale.
GNU -t SET1 truncation and SET2 indefinite repeat with a trailing element.
Invalid character class and unknown option diagnostics/status.
Empty stdin, short replacement extension, translate-before-squeeze ordering and surplus deletion operands.
exclusions: Multibyte and locale-specific character semantics are not covered; parity fixtures intentionally run in LC_ALL=C.
No in-place file operation is applicable: tr transforms stdin to stdout.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash contract that tr is registered as a builtin and its help entry is available, without counting this as operation parity.
Translate an ASCII range while leaving nonmembers and blank lines unchanged.
Translate the POSIX lower class to upper and preserve digits and existing uppercase bytes.
Delete NUL bytes selected by an octal escape while retaining surrounding bytes and the final newline.
Squeeze repeated spaces and tabs from the POSIX blank class, including separate adjacent runs.
Delete bytes outside alphanumeric-or-space and then squeeze the surviving spaces.
Translate a three-byte octal range and preserve an input byte outside the range.
Translate the complement of one byte in the C locale, covering NUL and 0xff and the default final-character extension of SET2.
Check GNU -t truncation: only the first two members of SET1 translate when SET2 has two characters.
Check GNU SET2 [c*] padding while reserving a trailing explicit replacement character.
A misspelled POSIX character class must fail with a diagnostic instead of silently translating literal bracket text.
An unsupported option must be rejected with a diagnostic; this also checks the externally visible status code against GNU tr.
